summary: That's an $8 million hike over 2025.
body: Remember when Battlefield 6 dropped in 2025 and it was a big hit, selling seven million copies in three days and becoming the first Battlefield game to outsell a competing Call of Duty? And then Electronic Arts rewarded the people who made it by laying them off ? And also laid off the entire team working on an all-new, more story-focused game in the series? I remind you of all this—and, since we're on the topic, of former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah's recent characterization of the company as " a hedge fund with a videogame hobby "—because EA released its Form 10-K/A SEC filing yesterday, revealing among other things that CEO Andrew Wilson's "total compensation" for the company's 2026 fiscal year was $38,649,984, an $8 million increase over his 2025 pay driven in no small part by the success of Battlefield 6. title: Silent Hill: Townfall takes place in 'the perfect storm'—a remote Scottish town that stands on the edge of the age of the internet
summary: The internet has been a pretty scary experience for me.
body: What a fantastic time to be a horror fan. We've got the most amazing films coming every which-way, countless new indie games to enjoy, and the revitalisation of some of the best horror series gaming has, one of which being Silent Hill with its upcoming game Silent Hill: Townfall . Part of Silent Hill's revitalisation is a trend of mainline games which take the Silent Hill story and explore it in new locations. Last year we got Silent Hill f which took fans to 1960s rural Japan—exploring the purgatory between tradition and modernity—and this year we have Silent Hill: Townfall set in 1996 St. Amelia, Scotland. What will this game explore? Well, director Jon McKellan gives us some hints. (Image credit: Konami) There are some "very specific reasons why the game is set in this era", McKellan explains in an interview with Eurogamer . "One, that it is on the cusp of when technology started to explode in the home. We started to get the internet. But also who Simon is, the time it's taking place in, the type of town that it's in—all these things are kind of deeply relevant. title: The next game on GOG's preservation list would be your favourite ARPG if it hadn't released the same year as Diablo 2, and it's on sale now
summary: Opportunity NOX twice.
body: Ah, NOX. Poor NOX. Westwood's 2000 ARPG last graced our pages three years ago, as one of eight PC gaming classics that are still worth playing today , where Russell Adderson wrote that it "might have been everyone’s favorite ARPG" had it not, you know, come out in the year 2000—just a few months before Diablo 2. Alas, that's how it shook out. But hey, it looks like NOX is getting a second chance over a quarter of a century on: GOG has announced it won its latest patron poll to choose a game to induct into its Preservation Program—meaning GOG will commit to keeping the game supported and easy-to-run from now until the end of all things. Or at least the end of GOG. It was not an especially close-run thing. The games patrons could vote to induct into the program were: Lands of Lore 1 + 2, Might and Magic 7: For Blood and Honor, Silver, Albion, and NOX. title: One Redditor spent four months building a 'Turkish kebab PC' with working spinning components
summary: I'd love a byte.
body: Turkish kebab PC from r/pcmasterrace Though I don't know if I like the idea of getting a little hungry every time I see my PC, I can say I'm kind of in love with the Turkish kebab PC that user Zestyclose-Salad-290 has shown off over on the PCMR Subreddit . And that's because it's truly weird one-of-a-kind. For those unlucky enough to have never had a Turkish kebab, it is a mixture of meat placed on a rotisserie, and a carver is used to cut it up into small strips. In the PC homage, there is a spinning fan, GPU, motherboard, and PSU inside a glass case, with four fans at the bottom and four fans at the top to control the temps. The pole in the center of the build has an RGB strip around it, illuminating all the hardware. It's a truly ridiculous build, and one I'd assume was purely for show, if the creator didn't also post it on builds.gg , a PC building website, to explain the methodology. The build is kitted out with a Ryzen 5 3600X, 16 GB of DDR 4 memory, an MSI RTX 3070 Super and 1 TB of SSD storage. title: The latest ugly-cool immersive sim is scratching my itch for new Deus Ex
summary: And it lets you drive, which feels somehow momentous.
body: There's something defiant about the trend of deliberately ugly immersive sims. It is a statement: mechanics are king and beauty is a distraction, so here is something we scraped out of the vents on a PlayStation 1. I admire it. Not the graphics; the graphics look awful. I admire the sentiment. The latest in this proud tradition is Parkside: Decayed Soul Manipulation (in environments not restricted by the PC Gamer style guide, that title is rendered in all caps) from Banana Hardsoft, which releases on the 31st of July but has a demo you can play right now. It's got a System Shock start with a Deus Ex finish: you're Alexander, a hacker in a rundown world where the billboards blare messages like "Do Not Hinder Law Enforcement". You hack a little too deep and men with guns kick down your door. It's not System Shock's Trioptimum Corp, though, it's a gang of zealots set up like the Catholic Illuminati. They strap you into a machine that lets you remotely pilot a combat-ready body and send you off to kill a man. It's all part of the ineffable plan to serve the Divine Rod. Or something. It's all very aesthetically piquant , even if Parkside deliberately keeps its plot mysterious by commun…

title: Yoshi-P is looking into ways to make FF14's 5 expansions and hundreds of hours less daunting for new players
summary: As it stands, the game's an awful big commitment.
body: Final Fantasy 14 may be an MMO, but it's certainly never sacrificed the series' talent for excellent storytelling. It's stuffed with incredible worldbuilding, a cherished cast of characters, and heart-wrenching story beats that'll get players shedding a tear from just hearing a few notes from a song that played during a cutscene. It is, however, also a story that requires hundreds of hours to experience the full breadth of its narrative—spread across A Realm Reborn and five meaty expansions, with a sixth one on the way. While Square Enix has pruned quests here and there in an attempt to streamline the experience, it's still a helluva lot of game to ask a new player to commit to. I've had the good fortune to be playing since the beginning, but I can say with absolute certainty that if I was only just starting the game, I'd be damn near paralysed by how daunting the new player experience is— especially if you want to play with friends who are already across the finish line. title: Subnautica 2 is responsible for Krafton's 'record second quarter performance' despite the messy legal battle and accusations of sabotage
summary: But it's also come with a cost.
body: Subnautica 2 might be a chill survival game, but the journey to May's early access launch was filled with drama, legal battles and accusations of sabotage. Just recalling it all is giving me a massive headache, which I'm now going to give to you. In 2025, Krafton ousted Unknown World's leadership and delayed Subnautica 2's early access launch. The publisher accused the studio heads of abandoning the game , who then fired back and accused Krafton of delaying Subnautica 2 so it wouldn't have to pay a promised $250 million earnout —a strategy Krafton's CEO came up with thanks to ChatGPT . The result of the dispute was a judge forcing Krafton to reinstate Unknown Worlds CEO Ted Gill and extend the earnout period . But the drama wasn't over. Krafton then almost immediately announced an imminent early access release date, which Gill believed was its final attempt to sabotage the game and avoid paying what was promised. It's genuinely a miracle that after all of this Subnautica 2 launched and it was really, really good. Earlier this month, it hit a new milestone: 5 million copies sold . title: Linux kernel patch can boost the Steam Deck's 1% low frame rate by as much as 31% in early testing
summary: There's life in the old handheld yet.
body: A number of recent Linux driver patches has reportedly resulted in significant performance gains for the Steam Deck . Valve's handheld runs on the Linux-based SteamOS, and these patches can apparently improve the Steam Deck's 1% low frame rates by as much as 31%. A fresh 'epp_boost' feature for the AMD P-State driver is largely responsible for the performance boost. David Vernet, a Linux kernel hacker at Meta, is the developer behind it. The feature implements per-core Energy Performance Preference (EPP) for AMD CPUs. As far as I know, it's not yet been reviewed by AMD's Linux kernel engineers, though Vernet explains via the Linux kernel mailing list that it was developed with gaming specifically in mind (via Phoronix ). Vernet offers a technical breakdown of the inefficiency these patches are designed to address, writing, "In active (EPP) mode the platform autonomously picks the operating point between min_perf and max_perf, biased by the EPP hint, and the kernel only rewrites the CPPC request on policy or limit changes. A workload dominated by one mostly-busy thread that takes frequent short sleeps (common in gaming workloads, for example) can fare poorly under this strategy." H…

My sentiment at the time could be summed up as: hey, this is cool. Well, I've now played a chunk of GOG's dolled-up Thief, and my sentiment can now be summed up as: hey, this is cool. No, really. I've spent a bit of my workday going through Thief's opening Bafford's Manor mission, and I'm genuinely impressed by how well a technically un-remastered version of Thief holds up in the big '26. It's not radical—you'll have to wait for Nightdive's effort for your proper bells and whistles—but it is remarkable. summary: It's good to see that at least someone's doing well.
body: Capcom just released its Q1 2026 financial report , and to absolutely no one's surprise, the company is doing well, really well. But to my surprise, so is Pragmata . As part of the report Capcom shared sales figures for its recent releases, and Pragmata sold more than 2.5 million copies since it was released earlier this year. Now, to be clear this isn't because I think Pragmata is a bad game—I liked its old-timey shooter vibes and QTE hacking when I played its preview way back when. And Justin Wagner really loved its puzzles, main duo, and "poignant" narrative moments in our Pragmata review . But even still it's a completely new story from Capcom with no existing fanbase to go to bat for it. (Image credit: Capcom) I also felt that its release fell a little flat as hype seemingly petered out rather quickly—I certainly didn't feel the need to tell the world about my adventures around the collapsing moonbase. Nevertheless, I'm happy that Pragmata was successful and that it translated into healthy sales numbers. Hopefully this gives Capcom renewed confidence when it comes to pursuing new worlds and ideas. title: You can now play Morrowind entirely in your browser: 'Honestly just wanted to see if it could be done'
summary: Good if you've got some downtime at work. On your lunch break, of course.
body: With Bethesda making us wait going on 15 long years for the next Elder Scrolls game (I'm not including Oblivion Remastered ), we've been left to our own devices. A phenomenon I've noticed spike as of late is calls for a Morrowind remaster, and a lot of chatter surrounding Bethesda's seminal 2002 RPG in general, like game devs weighing in on how it would fare if it came out today , and the history behind The Lusty Argonian Maid . We're all getting cabin fever. To make up for it not being ported to every platform in existence like its older sibling Skyrim, crafty Reddit user Dumpster Buddy (as spotted by Eurogamer ) has somehow managed to get Morrowind running in your browser . "I got OpenMW (the open-source Morrowind engine) compiling to WebAssembly," they explain, "so the whole game runs in a browser tab now. You open a link and you're standing in Seyda Neen. No install, no launcher." The most baffling detail is that it's the actual game engine flowing through your browser, "not a stream and not an emulator." body: Final Fantasy 14 has become just as much of a social chatroom as it has an MMO. That playstyle has led to an increasing demand for more flexibility and freedom in the way players can present their characters over the years which, for a long time, was met with a fair bit of resistance from director and producer Naoki Yoshida. title: Next year's Fallout 76 major expansion will explore a 'prequel story to Fallout 3'
summary: Players will be able to venture forth into Raven Rock next year.
body: A few weeks ago Bethesda Studios hit the big red button and announced that both Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas remasters are in pre-production, but that wasn't all—there was also news of Fallout 76's next major expansion. "Fallout 76 continues to be home to millions of players exploring Appalachia together," an official news post from Bethesda explains. "With nearly 70 free updates released to date, the journey is far from over. In fact, we have a major Fallout 76 expansion planned for next year; Raven Rock, a prequel story to Fallout 3." (Image credit: Bethesda) The last major expansion for Fallout 76 saw players venture to Ohio for the first time in Fallout lore in the Burning Springs expansion. Released around the Fallout TV show's season 2, Burning Springs was meant to marry the game with the show and its Fallout 3/ New Vegas inspirations ; aka, "desert, deathclaws, and raiders." But if Raven Rock is going to be a Fallout 3 prequel then, first off, it's going to be a very early one: 76 takes place over 100 years before Fallout 3. Secondly it'll venture over to the other side of the map, as it'll probably head to the Capital Wasteland—which is east of Vault 76—specifically to …

title: Marvel Tōkon's developer has apologised to PC players for the beta's performance issues, with only a week until launch
summary: But it still broke fighting game beta records on Steam.
body: The Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls beta was open for just a short three-day window, but in that time it ran into an unfortunate number of issues. For one, the playtest for Sony's exclusive tag fighter launched the same day PlayStation Network decided it would kick the bucket, shutting all services offline for almost the entire first day in some regions. We PC players were hit with another major issue: intense stuttering and all-round shoddy optimisation that got in the way of the otherwise slick and stylish combat no matter your specs. I think I'm one of the lucky few who actually had pretty flawless performance. One player even took to Reddit to call it "one of the worst PC ports" in a while: "This shit is inexcusable. Not buying until this gets fixed but at this point, I have no idea how you can get this cleaned up in two weeks." title: Consumer electronics companies were already worried about securing memory next year—now, supply is predicted to plummet by 70%
summary: No end in sight.
body: If you've been keeping up to date with news of the raging memory supply crisis , then I don't need to tell you how the AI industry's seemingly bottomless hunger for both system storage and RAM has significantly raised prices. Well, it turns out it can get worse than runaway costs, as manufacturers are even more concerned about securing supply, period . Apacer CEO C.K. Chang recently warned that memory shortages are expected to remain severe throughout 2026. He recently explained that securing supply is a bigger operational risk to Apacer now than paying high costs, as he expects memory manufacturers will release about 30% of their 2026 supply volume in 2027 (via DigiTimes ). Chang clarified that next year's limited supply won't be due to a fundamental shift in the market's structure. Still, in order to guard against such a shortfall, Apacer will attempt to secure as much inventory as it possibly can now. At the end of the 2026's first half, Apacer already held about $383 million worth of inventory. Many other consumer electronics companies are already thinking along similar lines, securing multi-year supply contracts and further ensuring the memory shortage won't ease in the near …

title: Nioh 3's first DLC hits in August, brings new weapons, a trip to the (sort of) future, and there's a mega-hard difficulty mode for the sickos
summary: Are you sickos?
body: I will be truthful: if you grabbed me by the lapels and demanded I tell you when Nioh 3 came out, I would answer something along the lines of 'the late 1980s'. The fact that the third Nioh—a rather good game, per our 90% Nioh 3 review —only released in February of this year feels like a weft in the tapestry of space-time. But so it was, and so it is that Nioh 3 will, on August 19, get its first DLC in the form of Hell Rising : "Our protagonist and appointed shogun, Takechiyo, journeys through time and is led to Edo in the future by an unknown yokai he met in his dreams," goes the blurb. "Edo in the future" is the year 1651, by the by. Things aren't looking great. "The large castle town that was once proof of the shogunate’s authority has transformed into a hellish wasteland plagued by the gales of the Crucible," rumbles the DLC description. "Yokai, human rebels, and alchemists from foreign lands have descended on Edo, creating a battlefield fraught with chaos." I knew a guy in uni who called himself an alchemist from foreign lands, but he was just a Latvian guy who sold cannabis. The new DLC brings new gear with it. Hell Rising brings the hoko and shield and ninja hoko and shield.…

title: Alienware 34 AW3426DW review
summary: Alienware's updated 34-inch ultrawide OLED monitor is even more awesome than the original.
body: Can it really be well over four years since Alienware rolled out the AW3423DW , the first mainstream OLED gaming monitor? The AW3423DW wasn't perfect, but by many important gaming metrics, it absolutely monstered every LCD-based display. That model, of course, was a 34-inch ultrawide and now Alienware has released its most significant update yet for that form factor, the Alienware 34 AW3426DW . So, what does four years of OLED gaming monitor development buy you? In really simple terms, some new threads, a bit more brightness, and a higher refresh rate. But when you dig down into the details, there's way more going on here. Most importantly, Alienware has upgraded to Samsung's very latest QD-OLED panel tech, known as Penta Tandem. In terms of headline specs, that means a bump from 250 nits full-screen and 1,000 nits peak HDR brightness of that OG Alienware OLED, to 300 nits and 1,300 nits respectively. You also get an upgrade from VESA DisplayHDR 400 True Black to 500 True Black certification, again highlighting the punchier panel. title: You won't have to worry about limited bandwidth or data now that Valve has fixed  local network game transfers on Steam
summary: Sharing is caring—here's how to check your Steam client is up to date.
body: One saving grace of a flat mate is setting up 'family sharing' on each other's Steam libraries at the earliest opportunity. Another saving grace is leveraging local network game transfers to then have a go at whichever game has become your roommate's flavour of the month, and judging them accordingly. Recently though, Steam's local network game transfers hadn't been working as intended. For instance, some folk would attempt to kick off a local transfer, only for Steam to download via the internet instead. That's less than ideal if your bandwidth is scarce or you're working with limited data. Thankfully, Valve shipped a fix to the stable channel of the Steam Client on Monday. That means, you should now be able to transfer games between gaming desktops, laptops, and handhelds like the Steam Deck once more—so long as you've got the most up to date version of the Steam client installed. Stick with me, because I'll tell you how to check Steam is up to date on your PC and Steam Deck. To check you're up to date on PC, open the client, click 'Steam' in the top left corner, and click 'Check for Steam Client Updates…' from the drop down menu.
